tile_reg.description: LinxISA v0.58 tile registers, retained by v0.58. 64 logical tiles are organized as T/U/M/N hands with 16 queue entries per hand; each active tile has dynamic descriptor-defined capacity under the per-thread total-capacity limit.
notes: v0.58 architectural tile register file, retained by v0.58: 64 logical tiles (T/U/M/N hands x depth 16).
Source tile fields in B.IOT are 6-bit values: T#1..T#16=0..15, U#1..U#16=16..31, M#1..M#16=32..47, N#1..N#16=48..63.
Single active tile capacity is descriptor-defined in the range 256B..256KB for normal non-empty tiles; imm4=0 denotes an empty 0B output tile.
All active tiles in one thread must fit within 512KB total tile capacity.
The legacy zero-based tile names are not canonical in v0.58.
tile_reg.physical_contiguity: each active tile occupies contiguous physical storage

notes: Deleted spellings and tile operations are assembler errors.

bitfields.description: Bitfield operations (BXS/BXU/CLZ/CTZ/BCNT/BIC/BIS/REV) parameter mapping and wrap-around semantics.

rev.description: REV performs byte-order reversal on the selected bitfield.
rev.invalid_n: If N is not a multiple of 8, the result is 0 (silent).
rev.operation: field = bitfield_wrap(SrcL, M, N); if (N % 8) != 0 then result=0 else reverse byte order of low N bits; high bits are zero.

bitfields.wrap_around: Bit ranges are defined on a 64-bit ring. For i=0..N-1, field[i] = SrcL[(M + i) mod 64]. Equivalent: field = ROR64(SrcL, M) & mask_low(N).

bru_control_transfer.description: BRU control-transfer instructions (B.* / J / JR / etc.) are not legal payload in coupled scalar blocks; they are vec-engine scalar-lane-only.

on_scalar_block_execute.name: ILLEGAL_INST
on_scalar_block_execute.note: v0.58 requires a precise illegal-instruction trap with TRAPARG0 set to the offending scalar-block PC/TPC; this rule is retained by v0.58.

contract_summary: Scope: vec-engine scalar-lane only (illegal in coupled scalar blocks => TRAPNUM=4 ILLEGAL_INST).
PC-relative scaling: offset is halfword-scaled (target = base + (sext(offset) << 1)).
JR: target = SrcL + (sext(simm12) << 1); SrcZero field ignored.
Predicate: B.Z/B.NZ test vec predicate register p (all-zero vs non-zero).
Faults: misaligned/unfetchable targets => E_BLOCK(EC_BFETCH), BI=1, TRAPARG0=faulting VA.
Body range: implicit/operational (no explicit architectural [BodyTPC,BodyEnd) boundary).
Operand registers: read scalar-lane GPR domain (not ClockHands).
vec_engine_scalar_lane.note: When executed in the vec engine scalar lane, BRU control-transfer updates the body-local TPC (not architectural global PC).

body_range.note: The fetchable body region starts at BodyTPC and spans the compiler-authored out-of-line body selected by `B.TEXT`. `BSTOP`/`C.BSTOP` and `BSTART.*`/`C.BSTART.*` remain legal body terminators when control reaches them, but an earlier lexical terminator does not by itself truncate the body if group-internal control flow branches to a later label in the same body. Targets that escape the current `B.TEXT` body region fault as `E_BLOCK(EC_BFETCH)`.

pc_relative.jr_alignment: No forced alignment; odd target is permitted (subsequent fetch may fault).
pc_relative.jr_srczero: The encoded SrcZero field is ignored (treated as 0) in v0.58, retained by v0.58.

tpc_invalid_target_fault.name: BLOCK_TRAP
tpc_invalid_target_fault.note: Vec-engine BRU targets that are outside the vec-body fetchable region (or otherwise not fetchable) are treated as body-fetch faults (not CFI).

tpc_misalignment_fault.name: BLOCK_TRAP
tpc_misalignment_fault.note: Use E_BLOCK(EC_BFETCH) for non-MMU body fetch faults (alignment).

predicate_register.truth_rule: B.NZ taken iff p != 0; B.Z taken iff p == 0
predicate_register.vector_predication: vector instructions are implicitly predicated by p

register_domain.description: Vec engine scalar-lane BRU reads operands from the scalar-lane GPR file (not ClockHands queues).

semantics: Every listed TLSU operation is an architectural memory operation in the same TSO domain as scalar load/store.
TLSU memory operations participate in aq/rl/fence ordering and must not violate store->store ordering.
Except for each MGATHER_CAS lane read-modify-write, a TLSU memory operation may decompose into multiple internal beats and is architecturally non-atomic to external observers.
Internal beats have implementation-defined issue order; software must not infer row or element beat order from one architectural operation.
Page and access faults are precise and restartable by software.
TPREFETCH performs the same reads, address translation, permission checks, faults, restart, beat decomposition, coherence, and ordering as TLOAD, but allocates and writes no destination tile state.
MGATHER forms lane addresses from the base scalar and unsigned u16/u32/u64 offset-tile elements.
MSCATTER uses the same address formation and writes the corresponding data-tile elements.
MGATHER_MASK and MSCATTER_MASK suppress memory effects for masked-off lanes.
Each active MGATHER_CAS lane is one atomic read-modify-write that returns the observed value and conditionally stores the replacement value.
GMOV is the TLSU Function 13 core4 collective global-memory movement operation.

tso_axioms: Program-order store->store ordering is preserved for all addresses.
A younger load may read from memory before an older unrelated store becomes globally visible (store buffer behavior).
Store->load reordering is only visible as allowed by TSO; fence/aq/rl tighten ordering.
No operation may observe a younger store from the same LXCPU before an older store.

notes: The v0.58 profile uses TSO as the architectural memory model, retained by v0.58.
The TSO contract applies to both scalar (BCC) and tile-memory (MTC/TLSU) channels.
A single LXCPU must not reorder committed stores (including TSTORE beats) ahead of older stores.
Shader-kernel bridged accesses (`l.*.brg` and `v.*.brg`) participate in the same architectural TSO domain.

notes: v0.58 system registers (SSR) and trap envelope definitions, defined by v0.58 unless explicitly noted.
v0.58 preserves the v0.58 ACR/EBARG/TRAPNO contract while integrating the reviewed v0.58 extension semantics.

v0.58 assigns SSR 0x0050 to BLOCKNUM and 0x0051 to BLOCKID.
Prior LB/LC SSR IDs are not reused in this profile without an explicit assignment source.
